mainTopic: נדה מה. – The age of three for a girl and nine for a boy: בתולין under three, two stories, and a new משנה about a nine-year-old and his יבמה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a debate: a ברייתא fits רבי יוחנן's reading of רבי מאיר, but the גמרא admits it is a difficulty for רבי ינאי. Next the גמרא asks about the משנה's line that under age three it is 'like a finger in the eye.' The question is whether the בתולין go away and grow back, or are never removed before three. A first practical difference is rejected by רב חייא בריה דרב איקא, and a second one about דם בתולין versus דם נדה is offered. רב חסדא then proves from the eye comparison that the בתולין go away and come back. Two stories follow. In the first, יוסטני claims she gave birth at seven, and the גמרא challenges this from the ברייתא about the three women who use a מוך. In the second, רבי עקיבא tests his students about a girl under three marrying a כהן, and the answer is that she is כשרה as a הלכה למשה מסיני. A new משנה then teaches that the relations of a boy of nine years and a day count legally, for יבום, טומאה, תרומה and עריות. The גמרא challenges whether a גט alone is enough for his יבמה, and רב's answer begins at the end of the amud.

steps.title: Setting up the comparison: רבי יוחנן's view fits the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא works well for רבי יוחנן, because there are תנאים who count part of a year as a whole year.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to רבי יוחנן: just as one תנא says one day in a year counts as a full year, another תנא says thirty days in a year count as a full year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It first shows that רבי יוחנן's view has no problem, so that in the next line it can point out that רבי ינאי's view does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that for רבי מאיר, a girl of two years and one day is treated like a three-year-old. רבי יוחנן can explain this with the idea that 'one day in a year counts as a year.' He also has a second תנא who counts thirty days as a year, so a 'partial year' rule is a familiar idea for him.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (opens a 'this works for X, but…' challenge)
A sage of the משנה period
One day into a year counts as a whole year
Thirty days into a year count as a whole year

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשלמא' is not a conclusion. It is only the first half of a challenge. The real point comes with 'אלא' in the next step.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan,
just as there is a tanna who says
one day in a year is considered a year,
so too, there is a tanna who says
thirty days in a year are considered a year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier debate on the daf between רבי יוחנן and רבי ינאי about רבי מאיר's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: Sets up the challenge to רבי ינאי's understanding of רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: First shows the ברייתא fits one sage, which makes it stand out that it does not fit the other.

steps.title: The ברייתא is a problem for רבי ינאי
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי ינאי, the ברייתא is difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי ינאי, this is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now makes its challenge. The ברייתא does not fit רבי ינאי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי holds that רבי מאיר requires a full three years. The ברייתא says clearly that for רבי מאיר, two years and one day is enough. So the ברייתא contradicts him directly.

keyTerms.meaning: But (turns the setup into a challenge)
For רבי ינאי it is difficult

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yannai, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'בשלמא… אלא' challenge that step 1 began.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's claim that רבי מאיר requires a full three years.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that for רבי מאיר, two years and one day is treated like three years, which goes against רבי ינאי.

steps.title: The גמרא admits the difficulty stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with one word: 'קשיא', meaning it is indeed difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is indeed difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not give an answer for רבי ינאי. It simply admits that the ברייתא is a real difficulty for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A one-word 'קשיא' is weaker than a 'תיובתא', a full refutation. The question stays unanswered, but רבי ינאי's view is not formally thrown out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; here it closes the topic with no answer

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן. רבי ינאי is left with an unanswered difficulty.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge from step 2 without answering it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא remains a difficulty for רבי ינאי.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: under three it is like a finger in the eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's last line: under age three, the act is like putting a finger in the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: Less than that age, it is like putting a finger into the eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the end of the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה compares it to a finger in the eye. The eye may tear, but it heals and goes back to how it was. In the same way, below age three the act has no lasting legal effect on her status as a בתולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than that (younger than three years and one day)
Like putting a finger in the eye: there is no lasting effect
The base text that the גמרא is discussing

phrases.english: Less than that,
it is like placing a finger into the eye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוחנן and רבי ינאי debate and goes back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Below age three, the act has no lasting effect on her status as a בתולה.

steps.title: What happens to the בתולין under age three?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask: do the בתולין go away and grow back, or are they never removed at all until after age three?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: these בתולין, do they go away and come back, or perhaps they simply cannot be removed until after age three?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the 'finger in the eye' rule actually works physically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both options lead to the same result, that she stays a בתולה. The difference is how. Option one: the בתולין are removed, but they grow back. Option two: they are never removed at all before age three.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before the חכמים
Signs of being a בתולה (the hymen)
They go away and come back
They are not removed at all
Or perhaps

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
these signs of virginity,
do they go away and come back,
or perhaps, as for being removed,
they are not removed until after three?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the rule quoted in step 4 actually works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the בתולין of a girl under three removed and then regrown, or never removed at all?

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two options.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: Both options give the same basic result, so the גמרא asks why the question matters in practice. This sets up the case that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to see a real halachic case where the two options lead to different rulings. Without one, the question would be purely theoretical.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference comes out of this?

phrases.english: What difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the question in step 5 matters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two options lead to different rulings.

steps.title: The case: blood the first time, none after age three
steps.stepSummary: Case: he was with her before age three and found blood, then after age three and found no blood. If the בתולין go away and come back, the reason is that there was not enough time for them to grow back.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example: he was with her before age three and found blood, then he was with her after age three and did not find blood. If you say the בתולין go away and come back, then the reason is that there was not enough time for them to grow back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a case where the two options would lead to different conclusions. It explains the first option here, and the next step explains the second option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the 'go away and come back' option, the missing blood after age three is easy to explain. There was not enough time between the times they were together for the בתולין to grow back, so the missing blood does not count against her. The explanation of the other option comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: He was with her (marital relations)
Within her first three years
If you say (testing one option)
Enough time (here, time to grow back)

phrases.english: For example, where he engaged in intercourse within three years,
and found blood,
and engaged in intercourse after three,
and did not find blood.
If you say they go away and come back,
it is that there was not enough time for them.
phrases.notes: He means: not enough time for the בתולין to grow back between the times they were together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by giving a case where the two options make a difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If there was blood before age three but none after, the 'go away and come back' option explains it by lack of time to regrow. Step 8 gives the other option.

steps.title: The other side of the first suggested difference
steps.stepSummary: If the בתולין are never removed until after three, then finding no blood after three means another man must have been with her. So which option is true?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say they are never removed until after three, then another man must have been with her. So what is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it started in step 7 by showing what the second option would mean in the same case. Then it asks again which option is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first option, finding no blood after three is fine: the בתולין just had no time to grow back. Under the second option, the first act under three did nothing, so the missing blood points to another man being with her after three. That is a real difference in practice, so the question 'which option is right?' now matters.

keyTerms.meaning: to be removed or taken away (here: the בתולין being removed)
they are not removed
another man was with her
what? (here: so what is the answer?)

phrases.english: But if you say:
that they are not removed at all
until after three years,
then another man was with her
So what is the answer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ: אִתְּצוֹדֵי הוּא דְּלָא מִתַּצְדִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the practical-difference answer begun in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under the 'never removed until three' option, no blood after three shows that another man was with her.

steps.title: The first suggested difference does not work
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בריה דרב איקא argues that even under the 'grow back' option, a wound under three might heal right away. Then she would bleed again after three, so no blood would still point to another man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא son of רב איקא objected: Who tells us that a wound made under age three does not heal right away? Maybe it heals right away, and then surely another man was with her!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בריה דרב איקא knocks down the practical difference from steps 7 and 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 assumed that under the 'grow back' option, there might not be enough time for the בתולין to return. רב חייא says that is not certain: maybe they come back at once. If so, both options give the same result, because no blood after three would mean another man in both cases. So this case is not a real difference.

keyTerms.meaning: he objected to it
a wound
comes back / heals
right away, immediately

steps.confusionAlert: רב חייא is not choosing between the two options. He is only showing that this case does not tell them apart.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya son of Rav Ika objected to this:
And who will tell us
that a wound made within three years
does not heal right away?
Maybe it heals right away,
and then surely another man was with her!
phrases.notes: Some versions add the word in square brackets, 'surely'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the practical difference offered in steps 7 and 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proposed practical difference, not the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the בתולין could not grow back in time, but they might heal right away, so both options give the same result.

steps.title: A new practical difference: blood both times
steps.stepSummary: The new case: he was with her before three and found blood, and after three and found blood again. Is the earlier blood דם בתולין or דם נדה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference is in this case: he was with her within three and found blood, and after three and found blood. If you say they go away and come back, this blood is דם בתולין. But if you say they are not removed until after three, this blood is דם נדה. So what is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first case failed, the גמרא offers a different case where the two options really do give different results. Then it asks again which option is true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the 'go away and come back' option, the blood found before three came from the בתולין, which is pure. Under the 'never removed until three' option, the act before three did not touch the בתולין, so the blood found then must be דם נדה, which makes her טמאה. Now there is a real difference in טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: the practical difference that comes out of it
they go away and come back
blood from the בתולין, which is pure
menstrual blood, which makes her טמאה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical difference that stays, so the rest of the סוגיא now tries to settle the question.

phrases.english: Rather, the practical difference is

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁבָּעַל בְּתוֹךְ שָׁלֹשׁ וּמָצָא דָּם,
phrases.english: for example, where he was with her within three and found blood,
and was with her after three and found blood.
If you say they go away and come back,
this blood is blood of בתולין,
phrases.notes: 'This blood' means the blood he found before she turned three.

phrases.english: but if you say they are removed

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא מִתַּצְדִּי אֶלָּא עַד לְאַחַר שָׁלֹשׁ —
phrases.english: only after three years,
this blood is menstrual blood.
So what is the answer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the practical difference that step 9 rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Blood found before three is דם בתולין under one option and דם נדה under the other.

steps.title: רב חסדא proves it from the finger in the eye
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא points out that the משנה could have said 'less than this, it is nothing.' Instead it compared it to a finger in the eye, which teaches that the בתולין go away and come back, just as an eye tears again and again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Come and hear: 'Less than this, it is like putting a finger in the eye.' Why teach 'like putting a finger in the eye'? Let it teach 'less than this, it is nothing'! Isn't this what it teaches us: just as an eye tears and tears again, so too the בתולין go away and come back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question from the extra wording in the משנה quoted in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה only wanted to say the act does not count, a plain 'it is nothing' would be enough. The picture of an eye adds something: a finger in the eye makes it tear, and later it can tear again. So the בתולין are removed and then grow back, which supports the first option.

keyTerms.meaning: less than this age (under three years and one day)
like putting a finger in the eye
and it is nothing
is it not that…? (introduces the proof's point)
tears up, sheds tears

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's proof: the משנה's eye comparison teaches that under three, the בתולין go away and come back, like an eye that tears and tears again.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: Come and hear,
'Less than this, it is like putting a finger in the eye.'
Why do I need it to teach 'like putting a finger in the eye'?
Let it teach: less than this, it is nothing!

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לַָאו הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן:
phrases.english: Is it not that this is what it teaches us:
just as an eye tears, and tears again,
so too the בתולין go away and come back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of steps 5 and 10 using the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the בתולין of a girl under three go away and come back.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's extra wording 'like putting a finger in the eye' instead of just 'it is nothing.'

steps.title: יוסטני asks רבי about the age for marriage
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how יוסטני asked רבי at what age a woman may marry. He answered three years and one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: There was an incident with יוסטני, the daughter of אסוירוס son of אנטונינוס, who came before רבי. She asked him: רבי, at what age may a woman marry? He said: three years and one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story (a ברייתא) in which a noblewoman asks רבי at what age a woman may marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's answer, three years and one day, matches the age the earlier steps have been discussing. This is the age when relations with her are treated as real relations in halacha. The story sets up her next question and her surprising claim.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story that really happened
Gets married
Three years and one day old

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There was an incident with Yusteni,
the daughter of Asveirus son of Antoninus,
who came before Rabbi.
She said to him: Rabbi,
at what age may a woman marry?
phrases.notes: She means: from what age is a girl fit for marital relations?

phrases.english: He said to her:
Three years and one day old.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בתולין discussion and brings a related story about the age of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl is fit for marriage relations from three years and one day.

steps.title: The age of pregnancy and יוסטני's surprising claim
steps.stepSummary: רבי says a woman can become pregnant from twelve years and one day. יוסטני answers that she married at six and gave birth at seven, and she regrets the 'lost' years.
steps.simpleTranslation: And at what age can she become pregnant? He said: twelve years and one day. She said: I married at six and gave birth at seven. Woe for the three years I lost in my father's house!
steps.whatsHappening: יוסטני asks a second question about pregnancy and then tells her own story, which does not fit רבי's answer. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gives twelve years and one day as the age of pregnancy. יוסטני says she gave birth at seven, so she was pregnant at six. She regrets the three years between age three and age six when she was not yet married. The obvious problem, that a six-year-old became pregnant, is what the גמרא will challenge next.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes pregnant
Twelve years and one day old
My father's house, meaning before marriage

phrases.english: And at what age can she become pregnant?
He said to her:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: Twelve years and one day old.
She said to him:
I married at six,
and gave birth at seven.
Woe for the three years
phrases.notes: She means the years from age three, when she could have married, until age six.

phrases.english: that I lost in my father's house!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with a second question and her personal account.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman can become pregnant from twelve years and one day, yet יוסטני reports giving birth at seven.

steps.title: Can a girl that young become pregnant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how יוסטני could have become pregnant so young. It quotes רב ביבי's ברייתא about three women who use a מוך: a קטנה, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can such a young girl become pregnant? Didn't רב ביבי teach before רב נחמן: Three women use an absorbent cloth during relations: a minor, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman. A minor, in case she becomes pregnant and dies. A pregnant woman, in case her fetus becomes flattened like a סנדל. A nursing woman, in case she has to wean her son too early and he dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges יוסטני's story by asking whether a girl of six can really become pregnant. It starts to support the challenge with a ברייתא about women who use a מוך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows a קטנה to use a מוך because a pregnancy could kill her. That means a קטנה is only a girl at the edge of being able to conceive. The lines that follow will give her exact age, and that is how the ברייתא clashes with a pregnancy at six. Each of the three women is allowed the מוך because a pregnancy would put her or her child in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: A soft absorbent cloth used to prevent pregnancy
A minor girl
A pregnant woman
A nursing woman
A fetus crushed flat, shaped like a sandal fish
She weans the baby off nursing

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking about רבי's ages. It is asking about יוסטני's claim that she became pregnant at six. The age of a קטנה that makes this a real question is given in the lines right after this ברייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא about the three women who use a מוך is a well-known source for when preventing pregnancy is allowed because of danger.

phrases.english: But can she become pregnant?
phrases.notes: This refers to יוסטני, who said she was pregnant at six.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתָנֵי רַב בִּיבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Bivi teach before Rav Nachman:
Three women use an absorbent cloth during relations:
a minor, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman.
A minor, in case she becomes pregnant and dies;
a pregnant woman, in case her fetus becomes a sandal;
phrases.notes: The worry is a second pregnancy that would press the first fetus flat.

phrases.aramaic: מְנִיקָה — שֶׁמָּא תִּגְמוֹל אֶת בְּנָהּ וְיָמוּת.
phrases.english: a nursing woman, in case she weans her son and he dies.
phrases.notes: If she becomes pregnant her milk could stop, so the baby would be weaned too early.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מִעַבְּרָה? וְהָתָנֵי רַב בִּיבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges יוסטני's claim from step 13 that she became pregnant at six.
steps.kashyaTarget: יוסטני's claim that she was pregnant at six and gave birth at seven.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats pregnancy in a קטנה as a borderline, life-threatening case, which suggests a girl as young as six cannot conceive at all. The exact age of a קטנה is given next.

steps.title: Who counts as the 'young girl' who uses a מוך
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא defines the קטנה as a girl from eleven years and a day until twelve years and a day. According to רבי מאיר, a girl younger or older than that has relations normally.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the 'young girl'? From eleven years and a day until twelve years and a day. If she is younger or older than that, she has relations in her usual way. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting רב ביבי's ברייתא and defines the age range of the קטנה who uses a מוך. This sets up the challenge against יוסטני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only in this one-year window is a girl able to get pregnant but still in danger from it, so she uses a מוך. A girl under eleven needs no protection because, by this view, she cannot get pregnant at all. That point is exactly what makes יוסטני's story hard.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl; here, a girl between 11 years and a day and 12 years and a day
Has marital relations
In her usual way, without a מוך
Less than this (younger than this age)

phrases.english: And who is the 'young girl'?

phrases.aramaic: מִבַּת אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: From the age of eleven years and one day

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: until twelve years and one day.

phrases.aramaic: פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן, אוֹ יָתֵר עַל כֵּן —
phrases.english: Less than this, or more than that —
she goes ahead and has relations in her usual way,
phrases.notes: Some versions add the word in square brackets; it means 'without a מוך.'

phrases.english: these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 14 by defining its term 'קטנה'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רבי מאיר, only a girl aged 11 years and a day to 12 years and a day uses a מוך; younger or older girls have relations normally.

steps.title: The Sages' view, and the challenge against יוסטני
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say every girl has relations normally and Heaven protects her. The ברייתא ends, and its message hits יוסטני's story: a girl under eleven cannot get pregnant, so how did she give birth at seven?
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: both this girl and that girl have relations in the usual way, and Heaven will have mercy, as it says, 'ה׳ guards the simple.' So how could יוסטני have become pregnant so young?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the חכמים's opinion. The גמרא uses the whole ברייתא to challenge יוסטני's claim that she gave birth at seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about whether the 11-to-12 girl needs a מוך. Both sides assume that a girl under eleven cannot get pregnant. That shared assumption contradicts יוסטני, who said she gave birth at seven.

keyTerms.meaning: And Heaven will have mercy (and protect her)
ה׳ guards the simple; people who act normally are protected from danger
Both this one and that one

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים. It comes from what both of them agree on: no pregnancy before age eleven.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Both this one and that one
goes ahead and has relations in her usual way,
and Heaven will have mercy,
as it says: 'ה׳ guards the simple'!
phrases.notes: תהלים 116:6. The ברייתא is being thrown back at יוסטני as a question.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא and brings out its force against יוסטני's story.
steps.kashyaTarget: יוסטני's claim that she gave birth at seven (step 13)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions in the ברייתא assume a girl under eleven cannot become pregnant. So a birth at seven seems impossible.

steps.title: Two answers: non-Jews are physically different, or she lied
steps.stepSummary: First answer: יוסטני was not Jewish, and the פסוק describes such people's bodies differently. Second answer: she was lying.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: 'whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys.' And if you want, say: 'whose mouth speaks falsehood and whose right hand is a right hand of lies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question on יוסטני in two different ways, each based on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer accepts her story but limits the ברייתא's rule to Jewish girls; her body worked differently. The second answer keeps the rule fully and rejects her story as untrue.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; it introduces one of two possible answers
Flesh of donkeys; describes a different physical nature
Spoke falsehood

steps.whatToRemember: יוסטני's birth at seven does not break the rule that a girl under eleven cannot become pregnant. Either she was physically different, or she was not telling the truth.

phrases.english: If you want, say:
'whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys,'
and if you want, say:
'whose mouth speaks falsehood
and their right hand is a right hand of lies.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים בְּשָׂרָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two alternative answers: one limits the rule's scope, and one denies the facts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יוסטני's story seems to prove a seven-year-old can become pregnant, against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Either the rule does not apply to her because her body was different, or her story was false.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a girl who had relations under three may marry a כהן
steps.stepSummary: A woman tells רבי עקיבא that she had relations before age three. He rules that she is fit to marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: A woman came to רבי עקיבא and said: רבי, I had relations before I was three. Can I marry a כהן? He said: You are fit to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא. It tells a story that shows how the law treats relations before age three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations with a girl under three are not treated as a real ביאה, as the משנה said: it is 'like putting a finger in the eye.' So she does not lose her status and may marry a כהן. Step 22 shows that this rule is a הלכה למשה מסיני.

keyTerms.meaning: A story, an actual case that happened
I had relations
The priesthood; here, marrying a כהן
Fit, allowed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows in practice that what happens before age three does not count as a real ביאה for marriage to a כהן.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was a story with one woman
who came before רבי עקיבא.
She said to him: Rebbi,
I had relations within three years,
phrases.notes: She means before she was three years old.

phrases.english: what am I regarding the priesthood?
He said to her: You are fit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאִשָּׁה אַחַת שֶׁבָּאת לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the יוסטני discussion and brings a new ברייתא about relations under age three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who had relations before age three is fit to marry a כהן.

steps.title: The woman's parable of the baby and the honey
steps.stepSummary: The woman answers רבי עקיבא with a parable. A baby cries the first two times his finger is dipped in honey, but the third time he sucks it.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: My teacher, let me give you a parable. What is this like? A baby whose finger was dipped in honey. The first and second time he cries out, but the third time he sucks it.
steps.whatsHappening: The woman from Step 18 adds more to her story by telling a parable. This sets up רבי עקיבא's new ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her hint is that it happened more than once. The first times were against her will, but by the third time she wanted it. This adds a new detail: some of it was willing.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable, a comparison story
Cries out, protests
Sucks it (the finger)

phrases.english: She said to him: My teacher,
I will tell you a parable;
to what is this matter comparable?
To a baby whose finger they dipped in honey.
The first and second time, he cries out against it;
the third time, he sucks it.
phrases.notes: She is hinting that by the third time, she was willing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה לוֹ: רַבִּי, אֶמְשׁוֹל לְךָ מָשָׁל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from Step 18 by adding a new fact about the case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She hints that the later relations were with her consent.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא now rules she is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: After hearing the parable, רבי עקיבא tells her that she is פסולה לכהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: If so, you are disqualified from marrying a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא changes his ruling. Now he says she may not marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18 he said she was כשרה לכהונה. Now that she says some of it was willing, he says she is פסולה. The new detail of consent seems to be what changed his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualified, unfit
The priesthood (here: marrying a כהן)

phrases.english: He said to her: If so,
you are disqualified from the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ: אִם כֵּן, פְּסוּלָה אַתְּ לַכְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the parable with a new ruling that reverses Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since some of it was willing, she is פסולה לכהונה.

steps.title: The students look puzzled and רבי עקיבא asks why
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא sees his students looking at each other and asks them why the ruling bothers them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw the students looking at one another. He said to them: Why is this matter hard in your eyes?
steps.whatsHappening: The students are surprised by the ruling, and רבי עקיבא asks them what is bothering them. This sets up their answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students' looks show they think something is wrong with the ruling. רבי עקיבא invites them to say what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Looking (at each other)
Difficult, troubling

phrases.english: He saw the students looking at one another.
He said to them:
Why is this matter difficult in your eyes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the students reacting to the ruling of Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is troubling the students about the ruling.

steps.title: The students say a girl under three is always fit
steps.stepSummary: The students answer that it is a הלכה למשה מסיני that a girl under three is כשרה לכהונה, just as the whole Torah is from Sinai.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Just as the whole תורה is a הלכה למשה מסיני, so too, a girl under three years old is כשרה לכהונה, and that is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The students explain what bothers them. A girl under three is fit to marry a כהן because of a law from Sinai, so willing or not should make no difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their answer works as a challenge to רבי עקיבא's ruling in Step 20. The law is a set rule about a girl under three, so the fact that some of it was willing should not change it.

keyTerms.meaning: A law handed down to משה at Sinai, not learned from a פסוק
Less than, younger than
Fit, allowed

steps.whyThisMatters: This states the practical הלכה: a girl under three is כשרה לכהונה either way.

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: Some versions add the words in square brackets.

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁכׇּל הַתּוֹרָה הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי,
phrases.english: Just as the entire Torah is a law to משה from Sinai,
so too, a girl less than three years old
is fit for the priesthood;
it is a law to משה from Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁכׇּל הַתּוֹרָה הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's question from Step 21 and challenges his ruling in Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A girl under three is כשרה לכהונה as a הלכה למשה מסיני, whether willing or not.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא only said it to test his students
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי עקיבא did not really mean she was disqualified. He said it to sharpen his students.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רבי עקיבא only said it to sharpen the students with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the story. רבי עקיבא's ruling in Step 20 was a test, not the real הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So there is no real argument. Everyone agrees with the students that she is כשרה לכהונה. רבי עקיבא wanted to see if they would notice the mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: To sharpen (the mind), to test

steps.whatToRemember: A girl who had relations before age three is כשרה לכהונה, even if she was willing. רבי עקיבא's opposite ruling was only a test for his students.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי עקיבא really held she was פסולה. The גמרא says clearly he was only testing his students.

phrases.english: And even רבי עקיבא did not say it
except to sharpen the students with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לֹא אֲמָרָהּ אֶלָּא לְחַדֵּד בָּהּ אֶת הַתַּלְמִידִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the clash between רבי עקיבא's ruling and the students' answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is that she is כשרה לכהונה. רבי עקיבא's ruling was only a test.

steps.title: New משנה: a nine-year-old boy and his יבמה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. A boy of nine years and a day who has relations with his יבמה acquires her, but he cannot give her a גט until he grows up.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A boy nine years and one day old who had relations with his יבמה has acquired her, but he does not give a גט until he grows up.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It teaches that relations by a boy of nine years and a day count legally for יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the topic was the age when a girl's relations count. Now the משנה gives the age for a boy: nine years and a day. His relations are enough to acquire his יבמה. But a גט needs an adult, so he must wait until he grows up.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the start of a משנה
His יבמה, the widow of his brother who died without children
He acquired her (as his wife)
A bill of divorce
That he grows up, becomes an adult

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A boy nine years and one day old
who had relations with his יבמה has acquired her;
but he does not give a גט until he grows up.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד, שֶׁבָּא עַל יְבִמְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A boy of nine years and a day acquires his יבמה through relations, but cannot give a גט until he is an adult.

steps.title: The nine-year-old becomes impure from a נדה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. If this boy has relations with a נדה, he becomes impure, and the bedding under him gets the weaker impurity of 'upper' bedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he becomes impure through a נדה, so that he makes the bedding beneath him impure like the upper bedding.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another law about the nine-year-old. His relations with a נדה count, so he becomes impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like with יבום, his relations count legally. He becomes impure from the נדה, and he passes impurity to the bedding under him. That bedding only gets the weaker impurity that the 'upper' bedding of a זב gets.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman impure from her monthly period
Bedding, something lain on
Lower, beneath
Upper, on top

phrases.english: And he becomes impure through a נדה,
to make the lower bedding impure like the upper.
phrases.notes: The bedding under him gets only the lighter impurity, like bedding on top of a זב. It does not become a source of impurity itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְטַמֵּא בְּנִדָּה לְטַמֵּא מִשְׁכָּב תַּחְתּוֹן כָּעֶלְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a second law about the nine-year-old boy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A boy of nine years and a day who has relations with a נדה becomes impure, and the bedding beneath him becomes impure like the upper bedding.

steps.title: The boy's relations affect תרומה and sacrificial animals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues listing the effects of a nine-year-old's relations. He can disqualify a woman from eating תרומה, but he cannot make her allowed to eat it. If he has relations with an animal, it is disqualified from the מזבח and is stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he disqualifies her from תרומה, but he does not make her able to eat תרומה. And he disqualifies an animal from the altar, and the animal is stoned because of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing what a boy of nine years and a day can do with his act of relations. Here it covers תרומה and animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His act is strong enough to cause harm: a כהן's daughter loses her right to תרומה, and an animal becomes unfit and is stoned. But it is not strong enough to give a benefit: if he is a כהן, his relations do not let a non-כהן woman eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualifies
The holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their households may eat
Gives someone the right to eat תרומה
The altar in the בית המקדש
Is stoned (the animal involved in the sin is put to death)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he is a full adult here. His act can disqualify others, but it cannot give the full rights an adult's marriage would give.

phrases.english: And he disqualifies
phrases.notes: If he is unfit for כהונה and she is a כהן's daughter, his relations stop her from eating תרומה.

phrases.english: but he does not enable her to eat תרומה,
and he disqualifies the animal
from being offered on the altar,
and it is stoned because of him,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of the legal effects of a nine-year-old's relations
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nine-year-old's relations can disqualify a woman from תרומה but cannot give her the right to eat it. They also disqualify an animal from the מזבח, and the animal is stoned.

steps.title: Forbidden relations: the adult is punished, the boy is exempt
steps.stepSummary: If the boy has relations with a woman forbidden to him by the Torah, the adult woman is put to death because of the act, but he himself is exempt because he is a minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had relations with any of the forbidden relatives stated in the Torah, they are put to death because of him, but he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list. In a case of עריות, the act counts fully for the adult partner, but the boy is not punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that his act is a real act of relations in the eyes of the law, so the adult woman is fully liable. He is exempt only because a minor is not punished, not because nothing happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Relations forbidden by the Torah (for example, close relatives)
They are put to death by בית דין
Exempt from punishment

steps.whatToRemember: The relations of a boy of nine years and a day count as real relations. They have effects on others, even though he himself is not punished and cannot give a גט until he grows up.

phrases.english: And if he had relations with one
of all the forbidden relations stated in the Torah,
they are put to death because of him,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the adult women he was with, since they are old enough to be punished.

phrases.english: but he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם בָּא עַל אַחַת מִכׇּל הָעֲרָיוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item in the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In עריות with a nine-year-old, the adult partner is put to death and the boy is exempt.

steps.title: Is a גט really enough once he grows up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה, which said the boy gives his יבמה a גט once he grows up. A ברייתא says a nine-year-old's relations count only like מאמר by an adult, and מאמר needs both a גט and חליצה. So how can a גט alone be enough?
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he grows up, is a גט enough for her? But a ברייתא teaches: the relations of a nine-year-old were made like מאמר by an adult. Just as מאמר by an adult needs a גט for the מאמר and חליצה for the זיקה, so too the relations of a nine-year-old need a גט for the מאמר and חליצה for the זיקה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It asks about the משנה's line that the boy can give a גט once he grows up, because a ברייתא suggests a גט alone should not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made it sound like the boy fully acquired his יבמה, so a גט would end the marriage. But the ברייתא treats his relations as only מאמר, which is a weaker, rabbinic acquisition. With מאמר, the Torah-level bond of יבום (the זיקה) is still there, so she would need both a גט and חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is a גט enough for her?
A rabbinic form of acquiring the יבמה through money or a document before full יבום
The Torah bond between the יבמה and the brother-in-law
The ceremony that releases a יבמה from the יבום bond
A boy of nine years (and a day)

steps.confusionAlert: A גט removes only the מאמר. It does not remove the זיקה, and only חליצה (or full יבום) does that. That is why the ברייתא requires both.

phrases.english: GEMARA
And when he grows up,
is a גט enough for her?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
They made the relations of a nine-year-old
like מאמר done by an adult.
Just as מאמר by an adult
needs a גט for his מאמר
and חליצה for his bond,
so too the relations of a nine-year-old
need a גט for his מאמר
and חליצה for his bond!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by challenging the first line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's line that the boy gives a גט once he grows up (step 24)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא equates his relations with an adult's מאמר, and מאמר needs both a גט and חליצה. So a גט alone should not be enough.

steps.title: רב begins to explain what the משנה means
steps.stepSummary: רב starts his answer by saying he will explain the true meaning of the משנה. The actual explanation comes in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: This is what the משנה is saying:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב is about to reread the משנה so that it fits with the ברייתא, and his explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase הכי קאמר signals that רב will not reject the משנה. Instead, he will show that its words mean something a little different from how they first sounded, so that it agrees with the need for חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means to say (introducing a rereading of a text)

phrases.english: Rav said:
this is what it is saying:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge in step 28
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that a גט alone is enough once he grows up.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still to come: רב will explain the משנה in a way that fits with the ברייתא.
